question: Which of the following helps Paramoecium move food to the specific spot in the cell to obtain nutrition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cilia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cilia** are hair-like structures that cover the outer surface of Paramecium.
 
• They beat in a coordinated manner to create water currents, directing food particles towards the oral groove.
 
• These structures aid in locomotion as well as in food capture and ingestion.
 
• Cilia play a crucial role in the feeding mechanism of Paramecium by transporting food to the cell mouth (cytostome).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parapodia**: These are paired, lateral appendages found in polychaete worms, aiding in locomotion and respiration.
 
• **Pseudopodia**: These are temporary, arm-like projections of the cell membrane in amoeboid cells, used for movement and capturing prey.
 
• **Flagella**: Long, whip-like structures that aid in locomotion for many protozoa and bacteria; they are different from cilia in number and beating pattern.
 
• **Oral Groove**: A channel on the surface of Paramecium where cilia direct food particles to the cell mouth for ingestion.
